item.title: ECC3: a global model for evaporation residue cross sections in the synthesis of superheavy nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.24444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present ECC3, an efficient model for evaporation residue (ER) cross sections in heavy-ion fusion reactions from light systems to superheavy-element synthesis. The ER cross section is factorized into capture, described by the universal empirical coupled channel (ECC2) model; compound-nucleus formation, given by the Zagrebaev-Greiner empirical Fermi function of the charge product; and survival against fission, obtained from a simplified HIVAP-type statistical-decay cascade. The capture sector is inherited unchanged from ECC2 and reproduces 348 measured capture excitation functions with a logarithmic RMSD of 0.29. A single set of model parameters for the formation and survival of compound nuclei is fitted to 60 measured ER excitation functions with the corresponding RMSD of 0.27. About 95\% of both the capture and ER systems are reproduced within a factor of four. Because the fitted parameters are constrained by light, medium-mass and superheavy systems rather than anchored to the measured superheavy region, extrapolation to unmeasured reactions is well controlled. The model also resolves the individual $xn$ channels. It reproduces the measured $3n$--$5n$ excitation functions of $^{19}$F+$^{188}$Os and the systematic charge dependence of the maximal channel cross section for $^{48}$Ca-, $^{50}$Ti- and $^{54}$Cr-induced reactions. For the three element-119 reactions $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk, $^{54}$Cr+$^{243}$Am and $^{51}$V+$^{248}$Cm, it predicts $4n$ dominance, with maximum cross sections of 13.2 fb, 2.64 fb and 1.56 fb, respectively.
item.dc:creator: N. Wang, Y. J. Duan, H. Yao

item.title: Extraction of All Partial-Wave Interaction Parameters via Femtoscopy: The Central-Force Case
item.description: arXiv:2610.24600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a universal femtoscopic method to extract the source size and central-force interaction parameters for arbitrary partial waves from experimental data, with the interaction parameters defined in the effective-range expansion. The method is based on the Wronskian determinant and is applicable to both the Coulomb and non-Coulomb cases. This approach is numerically verified against simulated neutron-neutron and proton-proton correlation data obtained from the Reid potential.
item.dc:creator: Renjie Zou, Sheng Xiao, Zhigang Xiao

item.title: $\Delta(1232)$ isobars and weak-interaction bulk viscosity in neutron-star merger matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.25224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary neutron star mergers probe nuclear matter at densities of a few times nuclear saturation density and temperatures of tens of MeV, conditions under which heavier baryons such as the $\Delta(1232)$ isobars may appear. Previous calculations of the bulk viscosity of merger matter have considered nucleonic matter, with and without muons, and hyperonic matter, but not $\Delta$ isobars. In this work, we extend these calculations to neutrino-transparent matter in which $\Delta$ isobars are present in strong equilibrium. We derive the relativistic matrix elements for the charged-current $\Delta\to N$ and $\Delta\to\Delta'$ transitions, evaluate all electronic and muonic Urca processes over the full phase space using the nucleon width approximation, and include the in-medium $\Delta\to N\pi$ width with Pauli blocking. The bulk viscosity is obtained from the coupled linear response of the electron and muon fractions about the finite-temperature flavor equilibrium. We find that the $\Delta^-$ takes over the negative charge from the leptons, which raises the proton fraction and opens the nucleonic direct Urca process. Up to about 3~MeV this change in composition, rather than the $\Delta$ reactions themselves, controls flavor equilibration. As a consequence, the resonant maximum of the bulk viscosity moves to lower temperatures for all oscillation frequencies we consider, and kHz density oscillations near resonance are damped several times faster than in nucleonic matter. We also show that, for nucleonic matter, the choice of the equilibrium state about which the rates are linearized shifts the resonance temperature by up to a few MeV at high density.
item.dc:creator: Bharat Kumar

item.title: Neutron-star dark-matter limits measure the maximum-mass headroom
item.description: arXiv:2610.25240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neutron stars constrain dark matter that is present inside them, through their maximum mass and the tidal deformability. The standard approach adds a dark component to one nuclear equation of state (EoS) and compares the stars with pulsar masses and with GW170817, so each limit inherits an EoS dependence that has not been quantified. In this paper we add a QCD axion and a $Z'$-portal dark fermion to the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model, in the formulation of the public code of Kumamoto et al.\ [Phys.\ Rev.\ D \textbf{112}, 043008 (2025)], and compute the stars for $257$ published RMF parameter sets from the compilation of Sun, Bhattiprolu, and Lattimer [Phys.\ Rev.\ C \textbf{109}, 055801 (2024)], with the dark matter either moving with the baryons or in its own equilibrium. We find that the stars constrain only the dark rest mass per baryon, and that its upper limit is the maximum-mass headroom of the EoS above the pulsar-mass bound divided by a quasi-universal rate, whose residual follows the compactness of the maximum-mass star; a compact dark core roughly doubles the rate, and the axion condensate barely changes it. Capture cannot supply the dark matter the stars could detect, and the portal reaches the EoS only at couplings disfavoured by anomaly cancellation, so a neutron-star limit on dark matter is a statement about the headroom of the nuclear EoS.
item.dc:creator: Probit J Kalita, Soham Singh, Pinku Routaray, Bharat Kumar

item.title: Deformability of neutron-deficient Sn nuclei studied with semi-realistic interaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.25647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although Sn nuclei have long been considered typical spherical nuclei, the $E2$ transitions in neutron-deficient Sn nuclei have posed a puzzle. We argue that their deformability may resolve this issue, based on self-consistent calculations with a semi-realistic interaction. The significant role of the pseudo-spin symmetry, which is attributed to the effects of the tensor force, is also discussed.
item.dc:creator: H. Nakada, Y. Omura, K. Abe, M. Takahashi, T. Inakura

item.title: Isospin-invariant Skyrme density functional investigation of quadrupole deformations in the isospin triplets of $\bf{A=70, 74}$ and $\bf{78}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we perform self-consistent isospin-invariant Skyrme density functional calculations to investigate the ground-state properties of the isospin triplets with mass numbers $A=70$, $74$, and $78$. The present study is motivated by the reported anomaly between the observed quadrupole deformation and that expected from isospin symmetry. It is shown that the trend of the deduced $T_z$ dependence of $B(E2,2_1^+ \rightarrow 0_1^+)$ transition strengths from the charge quadrupole moments is consistent with the measured values for the $T_z=\pm 1$ members of the $A=70$ triplet. However, the calculated $B(E2,2_1^+ \rightarrow 0_1^+)$ rates for the $T_z=0$ members exceed the experimental transition rates in all the three studied triplets. Our study implies that non-linear dependence of the $B(E2,2_1^+ \rightarrow 0_1^+)$ transition strengths is expected in all of them and primarily arises from the observed suppressed transition rates for the $T_z=0$ members.
item.dc:creator: Saliha Tak, N. Rather, J. A. Sheikh, S. P. Rouoof, S. Jehangir, G. H. Bhat

item.title: Heavy-quark thermalization in the quark-gluon plasma via a fractional Langevin equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamics of heavy quarks in the quark-gluon plasma is commonly described within a standard Langevin equation framework. In this work, we extend the conventional framework by using a fractional Langevin equation based on the Caputo derivative of order $\alpha$ with $1<\alpha\leq 2$. We solve the fractional Langevin equation and derive the corresponding {\textit {fractional fluctuation-dissipation theorem}} for the heavy quark thermalization in the quark-gluon plasma medium. We calculate the time evolution of the mean-squared momentum, mean-squared displacement, momentum distribution, energy loss, longitudinal momentum loss, transverse momentum broadening, and the nuclear suppression factor of the heavy quarks. The mean-squared momentum thermalizes to the same value for all $\alpha$ at late times, in agreement with the fractional fluctuation-dissipation theorem, and the nuclear suppression factor shows a systematic $\alpha$-dependence. The energy loss of an energetic heavy quark grows strongly with $\alpha$. The time evolution of the heavy quark momentum distribution provides additional sensitivity to the fractional dynamics of the heavy quarks in the QGP medium.
item.dc:creator: Jai Prakash, Mohammad Yousuf Jamal, Shanshan Cao, Guang-You Qin b, Yifeng Sun

item.title: Fluctuations of $v_2$ versus fluctuations of $\varepsilon_2$: Beyond linear and cubic response
item.description: arXiv:2610.26621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Elliptic flow ($v_2$) is the most prominent signature of collective flow in heavy-ion collisions. Its event-by-event fluctuations are accurately measured in Pb+Pb collisions at the LHC. They originate from the early stages of the collision, and are usually understood in terms of linear response to the initial anisotropy $\varepsilon_2$, with a small cubic correction. We reveal deviations from this scenario on the basis of extensive event-by-event hydrodynamic simulations. We analyze the hydrodynamic response order by order in the cumulant expansion of $\varepsilon_2$ and $v_2$ fluctuations. We carry out this expansion in the "intrinsic frame" where the magnitude and direction of the impact parameter are fixed. We find that the asymmetry of $v_2$ fluctuations is opposite to that of $\varepsilon_2$ fluctuations. We also find that the response to $\varepsilon_2$ fluctuations is larger by $\approx 10-20\%$ than the response to the average geometry. This effect, which is not explained by the cubic response, increases the splitting between $v_2\{2\}$ and $v_2\{4\}$.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kirchner, Mubarak Alqahtani, Jean-Yves Ollitrault

item.title: Trapped-ion quantum simulation of (1+1)D SU(2) lattice gauge theory via loop-string-hadron formulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a quantum simulation of the SU(2) lattice gauge theory in 1+1 dimensions with one flavor of fermions, performed using the trapped-ion Quantinuum System Model H2. This work is based on the loop-string-hadron (LSH) formulation of the gauge theory, and is distinguished by using qubits to represent both bosonic-gauge and fermionic-matter degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we access the $j=1$ electric-flux sector beyond the $j_{\max}=1/2$ truncation commonly used in SU(2) quantum simulations. To that end, we digitize an electric-field degree of freedom using a multiqubit register for representing the bosonic quantum number. Our simulation therefore synthesizes several key ingredients relevant to quantum simulations in higher spatial dimensions, in particular explicit local gauge-field degrees of freedom represented here by a multiqubit bosonic register, while relying solely on circuit-construction optimizations that are expected to scale polynomially with lattice size. This work demonstrates that modern quantum hardware is increasingly able to accommodate the features of complicated but physically important lattice gauge theories while successfully reproducing the expected Trotterized dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Toshiaki Kaji, Jesse R. Stryker, Yutaro Iiyama, Lento Nagano, Enrico Rinaldi, Christian W. Bauer, Koji Terashi

item.title: Electric Flux as a Criterion for String Breaking and Schwinger Pair Production
item.description: arXiv:2610.24175v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define string breaking by the midpoint electric field falling to half a flux unit. In the massive Schwinger model, an energy balance between intact string and screened configuration predicts this separation using only vacuum observables and meson masses as input. We observe numerically that this half flux point corresponds to equal weights of the two configurations thus explaining the observed peak of the entanglement entropy as maximal uncertainty of the binary flux. The same binary uncertainty explains the entanglement peak at the vacuum transition. Near breaking, screening organizes part of the spatial entanglement between the string interior and exterior into a nearly maximally entangled bit. Within the selected flux sectors, this approximate encoded Bell pair records whether the flux is screened and nearly separates from the remaining correlations. The vacuum transition exhibits the same structure. The string and the $\theta$-vacuum reveal a matching structure of the capacity of entanglement minimum at their transition point, linking their entanglement spectra. The transition rearranges degrees of freedom coherently as revealed by the entanglement asymmetry and Robustness of Magic of disjoint subregions. Finally, we construct the $\theta$-vacuum and string wavefunctions with high fidelity using a restricted Boltzmann machine ansatz.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Grieninger

item.title: Recent Advances in Transverse-Momentum--Dependent Distributions in Lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.24785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unraveling the three-dimensional structure of hadrons is a central objective in modern nuclear and particle physics. Transverse Momentum Dependent parton distributions (TMDs) provide crucial insights into the interplay between partonic transverse motion and spin, and are indispensable for describing a wide range of high-energy processes at facilities such as JLab, COMPASS, the LHC, and the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider. In recent years, significant progress has been made in accessing TMDs from lattice QCD using novel approaches. Methods based on ratios of Mellin moments, large-momentum effective theory (LaMET), and Coulomb-gauge techniques have enabled first-principles investigations of the Collins-Soper kernel, intrinsic soft functions, TMD wave functions, and TMDPDFs. Recent lattice results for both unpolarized and spin-dependent distributions, including the Boer-Mulders function, demonstrate the feasibility of extracting transverse-momentum--dependent information directly from QCD. This paper reviews recent advances in lattice-QCD studies of TMDs, outlines remaining challenges such as continuum and infinite-momentum extrapolations, and discusses future directions toward precision determinations of hadron structure in three dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Huey-Wen Lin, Wei Wang, Yong Zhao

item.title: Real-time quantum simulation of hadron production in deep inelastic scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.25350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a quantum simulation framework for meson production in deep inelastic scattering based on light-front QCD Hamiltonian formalism. A quark-antiquark dipole, prepared either as a single-momentum state or as the $q\bar q$ component of a virtual photon, is evolved in real time through the color field of a nuclear target via Trotterized unitary evolution. We consider both proton and gold nuclear targets, each characterized by their respective saturation scale. From the evolved state we extract the transverse momentum broadening, the total and elastic cross sections, and the $J/\psi$ production rate by projecting onto the $J/\psi$ light-front wavefunction. We then extract the nuclear modification factor $R_A$ at different photon virtuality $Q^2$ and analyze nuclear modification effect. Results of classical simulations show good agreement with analytical eikonal predictions across a broad range of parameters. For the single-momentum dipole, quantum simulation is demonstrated on a quantum circuit emulator with a smaller lattice size, and results are consistent with the classical benchmark. This work establishes a first-principles, amplitude-level pathway toward computing exclusive hadron production in deep inelastic scattering, directly relevant to the physics program of the Electron-Ion Collider.
item.dc:creator: Xianghui Cao, Meijian Li, Yang Li, Wenyang Qian

item.title: Statistical Analysis of Neutron Star Cooling: Implications for the Nuclear Equation of State and Nucleon Pairing
item.description: arXiv:2610.25427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We perform a statistical analysis of the thermal evolution of isolated neutron stars by confronting theoretical cooling curves with luminosity-age measurements for 24 sources. For each object, we explore five purely nucleonic equations of state (APR4, FSU2R, DD2, IST, and NL3$\omega\rho$) combined with representative models of neutron superfluidity and proton superconductivity, while varying the gravitational mass and envelope composition. The analysis spans approximately $10^5$ cooling curves. Within this framework, we find that only the NL3$\omega\rho$ equation of state and, to a lesser extent, IST, both including neutron triplet pairing, provide an overall satisfactory description of the data. The remaining equations of state are in significant tension with the observations. These results demonstrate that NS cooling provides complementary constraints on dense matter, alongside nuclear structure, global NS observables, and gravitational-wave observations, while probing the interplay between the EoS and nucleon pairing.
item.dc:creator: Afonso \'Avila, Ricardo Z. Ferreira, Violetta Sagun

item.title: Expansion schemes for finite density QCD equation of state: which one is the best?
item.description: arXiv:2610.25494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The finite density equation of state of QCD is a fundamental quantity for understanding the phase structure of the theory, and also for the realistic modeling of the QCD medium in simulations. While direct lattice simulations at finite density are extremely challenging, several expansion schemes have been devised to extrapolate into the QCD phase diagram. All of these schemes are based on susceptibilities of conserved charges, i.e. derivatives of the pressure with respect to the chemical potential(s). In this work we set out to determine which of these schemes possesses the best convergence properties. To this end, we employ extreme-statistics lattice simulations on a $16^3\times8$ lattice, which allow us to obtain susceptibilities up to order eight with remarkably small errors. We compare in particular two methods, based on contours of constant (normalized) baryon density and of constant entropy density. We find that the latter converges more quickly, effectively requiring susceptibilities only up to order four to cover the chemical potential range up to at least $\mu_B \approx 500$ MeV. We also extend the comparison to the three dimensional space of chemical potentials, and find that the entropy-based method consistently shows superior convergence.
item.dc:creator: Szabolcs Bors\'anyi, Zolt\'an Fodor, Jana N. Guenther, Piyush Kumar, Paolo Parotto, Attila P\'asztor, Chik Him Wong

item.title: Hyperonic Direct-Urca Neutrino Emission with Lattice-QCD-Informed Form Factors
item.description: arXiv:2610.25514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of direct-Urca neutrino emission in hyperonic neutron-star matter to the structure and momentum dependence of baryonic transition form factors. Using the zero-temperature FSU2H relativistic mean-field equation of state, we derive the relativistic emissivity for general spin-$1/2$ baryon transitions with the complete six form-factor contribution. We compare conventional static flavor-SU(3) couplings with vacuum lattice-QCD-informed form factors, using direct lattice vacuum input for $n\rightarrow p$ and $\Lambda\rightarrow p$ and a hybrid construction for the remaining hyperonic channels. Evaluating the latter both at $q^2=0$ and at the kinetic momentum transfer sampled at the Fermi surfaces separates changes in the zero-momentum couplings from momentum-transfer effects. The sensitivity is strongly channel dependent. The nucleonic transition probes $q^2\simeq0$ and is only weakly affected, whereas hyperonic channels can sample substantially larger momentum transfers and receive correspondingly larger corrections. These modifications propagate to the integrated neutrino luminosity of stellar configurations. Our results estimate the possible scale of the sensitivity coming from momentum transfer dependence, absent from static-coupling treatments and motivate future first-principles studies of baryonic weak currents in dense matter.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Konstantinou

item.title: Parton Fragmentation Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This chapter provides a pedagogical and comprehensive introduction to parton fragmentation functions (FFs), the essential non-perturbative quantities in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) that describe the universal process of hadronization, the transition of quarks and gluons into observable hadrons. Formally defined as gauge-invariant matrix elements, the determination of FFs is achieved through global QCD analyses that synthesize world data from three primary processes: electron-positron annihilation, semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering, and proton-proton collisions. This chapter covers the theoretical foundations of FFs, including their operator definitions and properties, the experimental probes used to constrain them, and the methodologies of modern global analyses. The discussion is extended to more advanced topics, including dihadron FFs, the three-dimensional picture of hadronization provided by spin- and transverse-momentum-dependent FFs, and the modification of fragmentation in a nuclear medium, which is key to probe their fundamental properties.
item.dc:creator: Hongxi Xing

item.title: Transverse momentum dependent parton distributions at small $x$
item.description: arXiv:2610.26004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distributions provide a three-dimensional description of the momentum structure of hadrons. They are probed in proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions at the LHC and RHIC, and are a central part of the physics program of the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). While TMD factorization is well established at moderate Bjorken $x$, the small-$x$ regime requires a different treatment, since large logarithms of $1/x$ must be resummed and non-linear effects due to high gluon densities become important. The Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory provides a natural framework to describe TMDs in this saturation regime and to connect them with standard TMD factorization. This chapter reviews quark and gluon TMDs at small $x$, covering operator definitions, gauge-link structures, and Wilson-line correlators in the CGC for unpolarized and polarized distributions. We discuss factorization for inclusive and diffractive observables, highlighting the role of process dependence and the emergence of a limited set of Wilson-line operators. We then summarize the evolution of these distributions, namely the resummation of logarithms of $1/x$ by the Balitsky-Kovchegov and JIMWLK equations, and of Sudakov logarithms of the hard scale through Collins-Soper-Sterman evolution. We also review TMDs beyond the eikonal approximation, including the sub-eikonal Wilson-line operators that give access to helicity and other spin-dependent distributions, their double-logarithmic small-$x$ evolution and the resulting asymptotics, and the sub-eikonal corrections to the eikonal distributions, which provide a first step toward the moderate-$x$ regime. Finally, we discuss phenomenological implications for present and future experiments, with emphasis on the EIC, and outline the theoretical challenges toward a unified description of TMDs.
item.dc:creator: Paul Caucal, Farid Salazar

item.title: Short-Distance-Free Leptonic $g-2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.26130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We note that the hadronic contributions to $a_e$ and $a_\mu$ are strongly correlated, which potentially allows one to reduce the uncertainties associated with higher-energy contributions (and address the current discrepancy between lattice and data-driven evaluations) by improved measurements of $a_e$ and the fine-structure constant.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Li, Vladimir Pascalutsa, Maxim Pospelov

item.title: KNO scaling violation: the role of the fragmentation region
item.description: arXiv:2610.26330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work is motivated by two independent considerations. The first is that KNO scaling is observed in the central rapidity region ($|\eta|<0.5$, for example) and violated when the fragmentation region is included ($|\eta|<3.4$, for example). The second is that, in the CGC framework, the $k_T$-factorization formalism is more appropriate to describe particle production in the central region and the hybrid formalism is more appropriate for the fragmentation region. The former contains small-x gluon interactions, where the latter introduce also collinear gluons and valence quarks in the dynamics. These two considerations put together raise the natural question: are collinear gluons and valence quarks responsible for KNO scaling violation? To answer this question we build a two-component CGC model which is able to reproduce the measured pseudorapidity distributions over all the available range as well as multiplicity distributions in pp collisions at LHC energies. With this model we find that KNO scaling occurs when the interaction is dominated by small-x gluons but is broken by the interactions including small-x gluons, collinear gluons and valence quarks.
item.dc:creator: R. Terra, A. V. Giannini, F. S. Navarra

item.title: The Israel-Stewart equations with a physical vacuum boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.26533v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish local existence for the nonlinear Israel--Stewart equations describing a relativistic viscous fluid with a physical vacuum free boundary. Compared with ideal fluids with a physical vacuum, the relaxation equation for the bulk viscosity introduces further derivative loss. The problem is compounded by the degenerate nature of the equations of motion on the free boundary. In this work, we construct solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces via a Nash--Moser iteration. Since the domain moves, the iteration is carried out in Lagrangian coordinates, while the linearized operator at each iterate is inverted on the Eulerian domain with the local well-posedness of the linearized equations established in our earlier work.
item.dc:creator: Runzhang Zhong

item.title: First observation of weak magnetism in neutron decay
item.description: arXiv:2610.26792v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weak magnetism, introduced by Gell-Mann as a hallmark consequence of the conserved vector current (CVC) hypothesis, has remained unobserved in the decay of the free neutron, the simplest $\beta$-decay system. The reason is that the relevant observable, the $\beta$ asymmetry, cannot separate the weak-magnetism form factor $g_M$ from the axial-to-vector ratio $\lambda$. We show that this degeneracy is lifted by combining the $\beta$ asymmetry measurements with the neutron lifetime and the $\mathcal{F}t$ value of superallowed $0^+\to0^+$ decays. Current data yield $g_M = 4.47(87)$, in agreement with the CVC prediction of $4.71$ and excluding the absence of weak magnetism at the $5.1\sigma$ level. Importantly, the significance remains between $5.0\sigma$ and $6.1\sigma$ for all considered variations of the neutron dataset, despite its well-known internal tensions. We further show that, under present experimental conditions, a full analysis of the energy dependence of the asymmetry would improve the $g_M$ extraction by only a few percent. These results constitute the first observation of weak magnetism in the decay of the free neutron nearly seven decades after Gell-Mann's prediction.
item.dc:creator: Miriam Camarasa-Domene, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez-Alonso, Mart\'in Novoa-Brunet

item.title: Bottomonium suppression in 5.02 and 8.16 TeV p-Pb collisions
item.description: arXiv:2401.16704v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the suppression of Upsilon(1S), Upsilon(2S), and Upsilon(3S) states in p-Pb collisions relative to pp collisions, including nuclear parton distribution function (nPDF) effects, coherent energy loss, momentum broadening, and final-state interactions in the quark-gluon plasma. We employ the EPPS21 nPDFs and calculate the uncertainty resulting from variation over the associated error sets. To compute coherent energy loss and momentum broadening, we follow the approach of Arleo, Peigne, and collaborators. The 3+1D viscous hydrodynamical background evolution of the quark-gluon plasma is generated by anisotropic hydrodynamics. The in-medium suppression of bottomonium in the quark-gluon plasma is computed using a next-to-leading-order open quantum system framework formulated within potential nonrelativistic quantum chromodynamics. We find that inclusion of all these effects provides a reasonable description of experimental data from the ALICE, ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb collaborations for the suppression of Upsilon(1S), Upsilon(2S), and Upsilon(3S) as a function of both transverse momentum and rapidity.
item.dc:creator: Michael Strickland, Sabin Thapa, Ramona Vogt

item.title: Zemach radii and nuclear structure effects in hyperfine splitting of lithium isotopes
item.description: arXiv:2509.01303v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nuclear structure effects are essential for describing hyperfine splittings from high-precision atomic spectroscopy measurements. These effects are often parametrized by the effective or elastic Zemach radii, with their difference being poorly understood. We show that the long-standing discrepancy between the effective and elastic Zemach radii in $^6$Li and $^7$Li could be resolved by taking into account nuclear polarizability effects in \emph{ab initio} nuclear structure calculations. Our results demonstrate that nuclear polarizability effects, negligible in ${}^7$Li, dominate in ${}^6$Li and explain the observed significant deviation between the effective and elastic Zemach radii. Furthermore, we show that the ratios between the nuclear polarizability contributions in different nuclei are universal in the limit of closure and SU(4) symmetry of nuclear forces. In particular, the nuclear polarizability contribution in an odd-odd nucleus is enhanced by a factor of $\mu_p/(\mu_p+\mu_n)\simeq 3$, with $\mu_{n,p}$ denoting the nucleon magnetic moments, compared to its odd-$A$ isotopes. The same mechanism also explains the Zemach radius deviations observed in ${}^2$H and ${}^3$He. These findings establish nuclear polarizability as the dominant source of isotope-dependent nuclear corrections to hyperfine splitting in light atoms.
item.dc:creator: Yilong Yang, Evgeny Epelbaum, Chen Ji, Pengwei Zhao

item.title: Semiclassical treatment of bottomonium suppression and regeneration in $p+{\rm Pb}$ collisions
item.description: arXiv:2510.03456v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bottomonium suppression in $p+ {\rm Pb}$ relative to $p+p$ collisions at center-of-mass energies of $\sqrt{s_{NN}}= 5.02$ and 8.16~TeV. Specifically, we combine cold nuclear matter effects (nuclear modifications of the parton densities, energy loss and momentum broadening) with those from hot nuclear matter (suppression and regeneration) by implementing the formation of a quark-gluon plasma in hydrodynamic simulations. Bottomonium transport in the quark-gluon plasma is evaluated semiclassically, employing two different reaction rates. The first includes quasi-free inelastic scattering and gluo-dissociation employing a perturbative coupling to the medium. The second is based on in-medium $T$-matrix calculations where the input potential is constrained by lattice quantum chromodynamics to extract the bottomonium masses and dissociation rates. These semiclassical results are compared to previous calculations in an open quantum systems approach and to the experimental data. Predictions for $\chi_b$ suppression at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 8.16$~TeV are also presented.
item.dc:creator: Sabin Thapa, Biaogang Wu, Ramona Vogt, Ralf Rapp

item.title: Time-Dependent Wave-Packet Approach to Reactions for Quantum Computation
item.description: arXiv:2603.26881v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe a method for obtaining the scattering matrix for nuclear or chemical reactions on a finite lattice. Aside from the preparation of the initial and final states as wave packets, the only other operation required is unitary time evolution, making this approach ideal for simulations on quantum hardware. The central quantity is a time-dependent overlap between incoming and outgoing wave packets whose Fourier transform corresponds to the scattering matrix at fixed energy, from which one can calculate elastic and inelastic cross sections for reactions involving two interacting clusters. Working in Cartesian coordinates enables an efficient encoding of the problem on quantum hardware via the first quantization mapping, with favorable qubit scaling for describing asymptotic scattering states. Within this framework, we describe a quantum algorithm for probing the scattering amplitude through different angles, including the forward direction, which provides access to the total cross section via the optical theorem. We demonstrate our methods through a series of numerical examples, for both elastic and inelastic processes, comparing against exact calculations. The techniques we describe can more readily be extended to a large number of constituent particles than other existing approaches, once fault-tolerant quantum hardware becomes available.
item.dc:creator: Evan Rule, Ionel Stetcu

item.title: Investigating forward-backward asymmetry in D-meson production and anisotropic flow in p-Pb collisions at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2606.28928v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the forward--backward asymmetry in the production and elliptic flow of prompt D0 mesons in proton--lead (p--Pb) collisions at$\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16$ TeV using the heavy-flavor improved string-melting version of the AMPT model. The model calculations provide a simultaneous description of nuclear modification factor $R_{\mathrm{pPb}}$ and $v_2$ in forward and backward rapidities. We find that the observed asymmetry arises from the interplay of initial-state cold nuclear matter effects and final-state partonic interactions, with the competition between coalescence and fragmentation playing a critical role in shaping the transverse momentum and rapidity dependence of both observables. This work suggests that a partonic medium is formed in high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions at LHC energies.
item.dc:creator: Siyu Tang, Chao Zhang, Liang Zheng, Renzhuo Wan, Zi-Wei Lin, Guo-Liang Ma

item.title: $^6$He structure from semiclassical 3D models based on $\textit{ab initio}$ spatial correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct semiclassical 3D models based on $\textit{ab initio}$ no-core shell model calculated two-body spatial correlations, which represent the preferred spatial configuration of nucleons for the ground state of $^6$He. We demonstrate that the presence of the two valence neutrons distorts and flattens the $\alpha$ core in $^6$He, marking a clear departure from the tetrahedral configuration of free $^4$He, and that the two valence neutrons and the center of mass of the $\alpha$ cluster ($\alpha$-CM) are roughly located at the three distinct vertices of an equilateral triangle. We compute the geometric parameters that commonly characterize $^6$He structure, 1) $\theta_{nn}$, the opening angle of the two valence neutrons with respect to $\alpha$-CM, and 2) $r_{nn}$, the root-mean-square separation between the two valence neutrons. Refining the model with uncertainty estimation, we obtain $\theta_{nn}= 58.5^{+5.4}_{-6.2}$ degrees and $r_{nn}= 4.12^{+0.37}_{-0.43}$ fm, agreeing with those calculated via a phenomenologically modified continuum-discretized coupled-channels method, while an interferometry experiment obtained a marginally higher $r_{nn}$.
item.dc:creator: Mengyao Huang, Tobias Frederico, Peng Yin, James P. Vary

item.title: One-photon annihilation of the bound electron-positron pair in the field of atomic nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2405.06720v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: One-photon annihilation of the bound electron-positron pair in the field of atomic nuclei is investigated. In our analysis the central atomic nucleus is assumed to be an infinitely heavy, positively charged and point `particle' with the electric charge $Q e$. The explicit formulas for the both annihilation cross section and one-photon annihilation rate $\Gamma^{(b)}_{1 \gamma}$ are derived and discussed. We also derive and discuss the closed formula which describes the angular distribution of the emitted photons. All our formulas can directly be used to evaluate probabilities of the actual one-photon annihilation in various atoms, ions and light molecular ions which also contain one (or two) positron(s).
item.dc:creator: Alexei M. Frolov

item.title: A New Bayesian Framework with Mass-Radius-Space Priors to Constrain the Neutron Star Equation of State
item.description: arXiv:2601.04294v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a new Bayesian framework to infer the neutron star equation of state (EOS) from mass and radius observations and neutron matter theory by defining priors that directly parameterize mass-radius space instead of pressure-energy density space. We use direct and accurate inversion approximations to map mass-radius relations to the underlying EOS. We systematically compare its EOS inferences with those inferred from traditional EOS parameterizations, taking care to quantify the systematic prior uncertainties of both. Our results show that prior uncertainties should be included in all Bayesian approaches. The alternative framework provides broader and more uniform coverage of the physically allowed mass-radius space, especially small radius configurations, with enhanced computational efficiency. Substantially reduced dependence on prior choices seems to result from having both prior and posterior distributions in the same observational mass-radius space. Results indicate that direct parameterization in observed space offers a robust and efficient alternative to traditional methods.
item.dc:creator: Boyang Sun, Tianqi Zhao, James M. Lattimer

item.title: Electromagnetic Backgrounds and Angular-Momentum Barriers in Gravitomagnetic Searches with Hydrogen-Like Ions
item.description: arXiv:2604.20717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hydrogen-like ions cannot usefully bound the gyrogravitational ratio $\chi$: in ${}^{95}$Mo$^{41+}$ gravity shifts the hyperfine constants by fractions of $10^{-39}$--$10^{-38}$ with the tensor structure of the hyperfine interaction, centroids cancel it, and the $2p$ lines are 1.3 eV wide. Isotopes with spin can, however, enter the King plots that search for new bosons: for the cadmium clock line, the second-order hyperfine shift of ${}^{111}$Cd is $-0.96$~MHz, and a specific difference with ${}^{113}$Cd reduces it to about $2$~Hz after calculable anomaly and third-order corrections.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo A. Pachon
